newsitem.title: USA: Brown & Williamson says suit dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Brown & Williamson says suit dismissed.

text.p: Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc, on Monday said a U.S. federal judge in New Jersey dismissed a tobacco liability lawsuit filed by four individual plaintiffs.
Brown & Williamson said the suit, Shirley Ehrich et al. vs B.A.T Industries et al., was filed against B.A.T Industries, Brown & Williamson and other tobacco companies.
The decision, by Judge Joseph Greenaway Jr, found that federal racketeering cases did not apply to the type of claims being asserted against tobacco companies, Brown & Williamson said.

"A significant part of this ruling is the judge's decision that the racketeering statute does not authorize lawsuits by smokers claiming health-related injuries," Tom Bezanson, attorney for Brown & Williamson, said in a statement.
The court dismissed the plaintiffs' remaining claims, citing lack of federal jurisdiction, the company said.

Defendants in the case were B.A.T Industries ; Brown & Williamson; Philip Morris Cos Inc ; RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co; Loews Corp's Lorillard Tobacco Co; the Council for Tobacco Research; and Tobacco Institute.
